stories.headline: NFL Week 5 uniforms: Packers debut Rivalries look, Patriots wearing throwbacks
stories.summary: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 5, led by the Green Bay Packers debuting their Rivalries look.
stories.body:
The Green Bay Packers have had their fair share of alternate uniforms throughout their distinguished history. There were the 1950s all-green look and the 1923 classic threads unveiled last year. However, no Packers combination has ever been like the ones they'll wear this week.

Green Bay will debut its "Rivalries" uniforms against the Chicago Bears on Sunday. It's a look that includes a desaturated vintage green jersey with alabaster pants and a matching matte helmet. The alabaster color is reminiscent of the aged paper of historic Packers stock certificates, according to the team. With the franchise being publicly owned, fans are able to become shareholders. More than 500,000 homes in Wisconsin include framed stock certificates, which inspired the uniform design. The alabaster jersey numbers feature an engraved treatment modeled after the lettering of paper currency -- a nod to financial support for the team. "Go Pack Go" runs on the back of the helmet, while "Making History Since 1919" is inside the collar.

In throwback fashion, the New England Patriots are wearing their "Pat Patriot" look versus the Las Vegas Raiders. The red uniforms include tricolored shoulder stripes with white numbers. White pants and helmets complete the look with the star of the show being Pat Patriot on the lid.

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey player buzz: Injuries to monitor and players to add this week
stories.summary: Fantasy hockey guide to the headlines around the NHL, including injuries to monitor and players to add.
stories.body:
We're only a few days into 2026-27 and teams around the league are already making headlines of both a positive and negative nature. Alex Ovechkin is calling it a career! Dylan Larkin is actually playing! Connor Hellebuyck is nowhere to be found! So let's take our first dive into this freshly-chlorinated pool of NHL news, which is heavily peppered with injury and goaltending items, with our goggles focused on any potential fantasy fallout.

Note: We're excluding ever-evolving injury situations that involve players currently listed as day-to-day, including Jake Sanderson, Mikhail Sergachev, Victor Olofsson, Josh Morrissey etc. Keep a close eye on your player news feed for those pertinent updates.

See more: Rankings | Projections | Mock Draft Lobby

Draft guide | Cheat sheet | October preview | Sign up

Florida Panthers

Aleksander Barkov (knee) isn't brutally hurt after all. First there was concern Barkov might miss most, if not all, of the regular season after doing just that because of a knee injury in 2025-26. No wonder hockey fans across North America exhaled when hearing one of the game's elite centers was then projected to return in 10 to 12 weeks, which was quickly reduced to eight-ish weeks, then more like six. At this rate, we'll see the Panther back on the ice next Tuesday (I'm being facetious). All considered, a positive report all around.

In less pleasant news, we're still awaiting an update on Brad Marchand after the winger slammed his knee hard into a goal post and left the ice without putting an ounce of weight on that leg. It looked bad. Fingers crossed Marchand isn't out long term, but I wouldn't heighten my hopes.

Advice: Place Barkov on IR and wait it out. I'd suggest picking up substitute top center Sam Bennett instead, but he's already largely spoken for in ESPN Fantasy leagues. As for Marchand, get ready to drop him outright if the news is as bad as all that. We should know in a day or two.

Colorado Avalanche

Mackenzie Blackwood is Jared Bednar's top choice in Colorado. We know this because the Avalanche's head coach has started the younger netminder instead of Scott Wedgewood in three straight games to open 2026-27. Which means we very well might not see much of Wedgewood outside of back-to-back situations, of which the Avs only have three this month. Of course, Blackwood can fall hurt or hit a rough patch, but we can't ignore Bednar's preferred approach from the onset.

Advice: Never mind his outstanding numbers from 2025-26, re-think relying on Wedgewood as a prominent No. 1 or No. 2 fantasy netminder this campaign. He might not play that much. Don't wait too long before swapping out the veteran for a more active goalie with perhaps a lesser team. Banking on Wedgewood eventually taking over once more could prove rather costly.

Winnipeg Jets

Connor who? While the former Hart/Vezina winner remains suspended, the Jets' active No. 1 is quickly enamoring himself to Winnipeg hockey fans. After a mediocre debut against the Bruins, Stuart Skinner is two-for-two, allowing just a pair of goals against the Red Wings and -- more impressively -- the mighty Avalanche. He looks sharp. It's worth remembering that, when at his best, this is a netminder capable of taking his team to consecutive Stanley Cup Finals.

Regardless of when Kevin Cheveldayoff trades Connor Hellebuyck, and to where, the Jets' general manager shouldn't feel as hard-pressed to get a top-notch goalie in return. Not when Skinner is performing this astutely behind a bunch of skaters who are producing themselves (see: Kyle Connor).

Advice: If at all unsatisfied with your fantasy goaltending, pick up Skinner while he's performing at the top of his game. As for Hellebuyck, keep him tucked on IR until as long as reasonably possible. Many oddsmakers still favor the suspended netminder to win the Vezina. Meaning there's a sense this standoff in Winnipeg might be resolved sooner rather than later.

Philadelphia Flyers
Michael Bunting is a Flyer. Not a jaw-dropping move, by any extent, but one that could pay out some short-term fantasy dividends. Frustrated with his club's start, and for good reason, Rick Tocchet can be counted on to jostle up his top six ahead of Thursday's contest in Ottawa. A group that might include the winger just signed to a one-year, $1.2-million deal. If only until Philly's more dynamite forwards get going. While Bunting isn't ever going to eclipse 60 points again, he has the wherewithal to put up a quick bunch in making a good first impression.

Advice: Add Bunting in deeper leagues in place of an injured skater expected back in the next two to three weeks. Edmonton's Zach Hyman, for example.

Edmonton Oilers
Devon Levi is the No. 1 netminder for the Oilers. Following a circus of a game in which he surrendered seven and still won in Vancouver, the 24-year-old has been better-than-solid in allowing three total goals through two victories against Seattle and Anaheim. Considering how poorly Tristan Jarry faired in the Oilers' opener, we can expect coach Mike Babcock to run with the younger netminder for the foreseeable future. At least until he struggles himself or Frederik Andersen (knee) is ready to return.

Advice: How desperate are you between the pipes? If more than less, and carry a fairly strong fantasy stomach, Levi could be worth a flier. Sure, Edmonton's defensive play consistently remains a work-in-progress, but this team is also going to score a ton. Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard already have 32 points combined through only four contests. Levi will be offered ample opportunity to win plenty of games.

New York Islanders

According to coach Pete DeBoer, Mathew Barzal (knee inflammation) is expected to return to skating Thursday. If all goes well, we might anticipate the forward's return to competitive play Saturday against the Lightning, or next Tuesday versus the Canucks (Thursday's tilt with the Blackhawks feels premature). Once again projected to lead the Islanders in production -- heavy on the assists -- Barzal remains available in about a third of ESPN Fantasy leagues.

Advice: After missing most of 2024-25, the ongoing knee issue is a bother. Still, Barzal played all but one game this past season, accumulating 72 points. This early, he's worth the health gamble if you need to replace another injured, or unpromising, skater on your fantasy roster.

Ottawa Senators

Linus Ullmark is "fine". At least that's the latest word from head coach Travis Green after the goalie was recently tackled by Bruins forward JJ Peterka. Okay. So, until we receive further notice, it feels reasonable enough to expect Ottawa's No. 1 to start against the Flyers in the team's home opener Thursday. If, however, Green instead opts to go with Samuel Ersson for a second straight game, I assure you Ullmark isn't entirely fine at all.

Advice: Keep a grip on Ullmark if/until the situation seems more grim. No matter what, there are better fantasy options around the league than Ersson.

Pittsburgh Penguins

Bryan Rust is back in business. Wrapping up his recovery from an upper-body injury through the Penguins' first three games, Rust celebrated his 2026-27 debut with three shots, a goal, and nearly 20 minutes of ice time. Splitting minutes between the Penguins third unit, and top line with Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell, the consistent shooter is expected to, once again, settle into the latter role. When fit and active, Rust serves as a well-balanced -- the extra blocked shots never hurt -- and underrated fantasy performer.

Advice: Grab Rust in all but the shallowest of leagues while tempering your fantasy expectations of Hendrix Lapierre. Losing his spot on the top line to the veteran winger, the Pittsburgh newbie falls to the third unit alongside Ben Kindel and Ville Koivunen.

stories.headline: Tottenham's Xavi Simons enrolls at Harvard Business School
stories.summary: Tottenham Hotspur's Xavi Simons has revealed he has enrolled for an online course at Harvard Business School.
stories.body:
Tottenham Hotspur's Xavi Simons has revealed he has enrolled for an online course at Harvard Business School.

Simons, 23, said in a post on LinkedIn that he had been accepted onto the Crossover Into Business Program at the graduate business school of the Ivy League university in the United States.

The Netherlands international is currently recovering from an ACL tear suffered during the run-in at the end of last season when Spurs narrowly avoided being relegated from the Premier League.

A timeline for Simons' return to action is unclear, but he is not expected to be match fit until at least the beginning of 2027.

He has been spending time in the U.S. while rehabilitating, posting photos on Instagram of him with basketball star Jay Tatum and watching a USC vs. Oregon college football game.

The Harvard Business School website says it has delivered the Crossover Into Business course to at least 20 athletes from the NBA, WNBA, NFL, MLS, NWSL and the UFC.

"I'm going back to school," Simons wrote in the post.

"During my recovery, I've been trying to use my time in the best way possible. Football is still my main focus, but I also want to keep learning and improving away from the pitch.

"I'm happy to share that I've been accepted onto the Crossover Into Business Program at Harvard Business School. It's an online program where professional athletes learn more about business alongside HBS MBA students.

"I've always been interested in more than just football. I want to understand the business side of the game better, learn from people in different industries and keep developing as a person.

"Over the last few weeks, I've spent time on both the East Coast and West Coast in the U.S., meeting new people and seeing different ways of working. It's given me a lot of new ideas. It also makes this experience extra special because of Professor Anita Elberse. We first met during my time at FC Barcelona, and later again at Paris Saint-Germain. We've stayed in touch over the years, so it was great to see her again and visit Harvard while I was in Boston.

"Getting back on the pitch is still my number one priority. At the same time, I want to use this period to keep learning and invest in myself beyond football."

Tottenham face Manchester United in their next Premier League fixture on Saturday.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look on the court in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

Oct. 8

LeBron to make preseason debut at Nets

ESPN's Dave McMenamin reported that new Philadelphia 76er LeBron James will make his preseason debut for the franchise on Thursday night at the Brooklyn Nets.

"The plan is indeed for LeBron James to make his preseason with the Sixers tonight against the Nets," McMenamin said on NBA Today.

Slater: The Warriors might finally have their man to bridge two timelines
ESPN reporter Anthony Slater wrote Thursday about Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who has impressed teammates and coaches ahead of the season. Here's a quote about Lendeborg from coach Steve Kerr:

"We're in a position now [as opposed to past seasons] where we can be thinking of development. Not just for Yaxel, but our whole group. We are not in the [championship] conversation. So let's see what we can do as a group to kind of reestablish what we stand for and how we operate and new beginnings in a lot of ways. All of that is really exciting to me. And Yaxel's a big part of that."

Oct. 7

Buss siblings formally file against Jeanie over Lakers sale
The legal dispute over the right to sell the Buss family's remaining stake in the Los Angeles Lakers continued Wednesday with five of the Buss siblings filing their case against their sister, Lakers acting governor, Jeanie Buss.

"Jimmy, Johnny, Janie, Joey and Jesse Buss, the five of six siblings who voted to sell the Trust's shares in the Lakers, today filed their formal opposition, demonstrating that Jeanie Buss's petition is legally and factually baseless," the siblings said in a statement issued to ESPN.

Windhorst on the growth of the NBA around the world: "I think the flow of international players into the NBA is even going to grow because of two things. One, the NBA is expanding to Europe. It's going to happen. I promise you. And part of the way that they're going to get everybody to buy in there is that they are going to guarantee investment in European players. This is going to be part of their sales pitch when they get it done.

"They're going to limit how many American players can be on there. They're going to expand their rosters because they're going to be playing in two different leagues, their national league and NBA Europe. And they're going to say, 'The reason you should care about our new teams in London and in Rome and elsewhere, and the existing teams, is we're going to develop European players.' And they are going to Europe for 20 years or more. They're investing in it like they did the WNBA. They don't care if it doesn't do great or somebody kicks rocks on it in the first year, they're going to invest in it.

"Secondly, international basketball is thriving."

Oct. 6

Porzingis injury timetable still 'indefinite'
ESPN's Anthony Slater reported on NBA Today that Golden State Warriors' center Kristaps Porzingis' timetable to return from an undisclosed health issue is still indefinite.

The ramifications of the Hukporti injury for Philadelphia
The season ending Achilles injury to Ariel Hukporti has roster ramifications for the 76ers.

Philadelphia is $1.8 million below the first apron, so they are not allowed to sign a player with their open roster spot until Dec. 4. The 76ers could create financial flexibility but at the cost of Jabari Walker, whose $2.6 million salary is guaranteed for only $250,000. Walker scored 11 points and grabbed 11 rebounds in their pre-season opener.

The 76ers do have an open two-way spot and can sign a player with three years or less in service.

Beyond starter Joel Embiid, Philadelphia's frontcourt depth is Dean Wade, Adem Bona, Dominick Barlow and Walker. -- Bobby Marks

Charania: Hukporti sustained a season-ending ruptured Achilles
An MRI confirm Tuesday that Philadelphia 76ers' center Ariel Hukporti sustained a season-ending torn right Achilles, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Hukporti will undergo surgery for the injury later today.

Doncic, who 'worked his butt off all summer,' lights up Kings
A lighter Luka Doncic scored an easy 21 first-half points in the Los Angeles Lakers' preseason opener over the Sacramento Kings on Monday night, needing only 16 minutes to sharpen up his game in a 127-103 blowout in Sacramento.
Doncic was listed at 244 pounds prior to the 2025-26 season. That dipped to 230 pounds entering training camp. The difference in physique from his heavier days is obvious.

"The guy worked his butt off all summer staying in shape and actually ran this summer," coach JJ Redick said. "He actually did like sprints and stuff. Came into camp in fantastic shape."

The Lakers were without Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler in the preseason opener. Reaves tweaked his ankle recently, and Kessler jammed a finger on the backboard. Both are listed as day-to-day. Without either, the Lakers still rolled through the Kings. Doncic scored all 21 of his points in a 73-point Lakers first half, resting while the backups finished the job. He made three 3s, four shots in the paint and got to the line for nine free throws.

"For someone who normally plays a ton of live basketball [in the summer], he didn't do as much of that by design," Redick said. "We've seen him literally every day in camp incrementally get more and more in rhythm."

Doncic badly strained his hamstring in early April and missed the entire Lakers playoff run while rehabbing the injury. He said he felt "great" against the Kings but downplayed any larger changes to his training regimen.

"I feel probably a little more rested," Doncic said. "I didn't play [on the Slovenian] national team." -- Anthony Slater

"You talk to other front offices in the league, they say the same thing. This guy is I mean, look, he's the No. 2 pick in the draft. Of course he's a stud, and he only got better as the season went along."

MacMahon on on Kyrie Irving's expectations in Dallas: "Masai [Ujiri] did not want to have any discussions about Kyrie trades this year. What I can tell you right now is Kyrie is fully on board and excited about coming back to play with the Mavericks.

"He just organized this kind of unofficial minicamp that they had out here in LA with the beach yoga in Santa Monica and the runs. ESPN NBA insiders Ben Golliver, Zach Kram and Bobby Marks examine both sides of the Towns-Knicks contract talks -- plus the deal our resident general manager would choose.

Oct. 5

Clippers' Strus suffered partial tear in right foot
During Sunday's preseason game, LA Clippers guard Max Strus suffered a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his right foot, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. He will be reevaluated in four weeks.

Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns not expecting extension soon
New York Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns said Monday that, "It don't look good" in regards to him and the franchise agreeing to a contract extension before the start of the season.

"Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said. "None of those things have come close to happening."

Towns is eligible for a four-year deal worth over $276 million.

"This is a growing cloud around the New York Knicks," ESPN's Shams Charania said on NBA Today. "So far, these sides are not close"

Oct. 2

Hawkins, Grizzlies mutually agree to part ways
The Memphis Grizzlies and guard Jordan Hawkins have agreed to part ways via waivers, allowing the 2023 lottery pick to find a new home in free agency, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

The move comes three weeks after arriving as part of a four-player trade with the New Orleans Pelicans for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson.

Hawkins, 24, averaged 5.1 points in 51 games last season and struggled to find consistent playing time in New Orleans' crowded backcourt rotation. The former UConn star played just 13.6 minutes per game, a significant decrease from the 2024-25 season, when he played 23.6 minutes per game and averaged 10.8 points per game.

Slater on the Warriors' options this season: "I think we mentioned it last time we talked about the Warriors, but think about what the Lakers did with LeBron. I know we just questioned some of the deals they signed, but the fact that they could sign all those deals was because LeBron James took all his money and walked away. So you could let Jimmy [Butler] somewhat walk away.

"The other thing is, Jimmy and the Warriors really are fond of each other and we'll see what he looks like when he does come back. Obviously Jimmy's going to want every dollar he can get, but there's a chance Jimmy and Draymond [Green] could take pay cuts next season, right? The market might demand that they do.

"Jimmy fits really well with Steph Curry. We've seen that. Draymond is another player that you're going to hear a lot of noise about in the first week of camp from the Warriors about shifting Draymond's role and some of the numbers last year. With Draymond and Steph Curry on the floor together, it was still plus-105 last year, still a good offensive rating,117.7, but the moment Steph's been off the floor, and last year he was off the floor a lot, their offense cratered when Draymond was on the floor and was actually OK when it was no Draymond and no Steph.

"I've had these conversations with Steve [Kerr] and again I think you're going to hear it a lot publicly in their messaging, they're going to adapt the offense at times away from Draymond. They're going to try to make him more of a spot-up shooter at times instead of giving him the ball. They're trying to limit his turnovers."

Oct. 1

Duren, Pistons end standoff with long-term deal
All-NBA center Jalen Duren has agreed to a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract to return to the Detroit Pistons, his agent told ESPN's Shams Charania. Duren had until 11:59 p.m. ET Thursday to decide on the Pistons' one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

Mitch Johnson excited about Billy Donovan's role with Spurs
San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson likes what he's seen so far at training camp from new lead assistant coach Billy Donovan.

"I don't want to be naive enough to think I'm going to tell you what a 61-year old Hall of Fame coach like Billy Donovan and his resume can bring to the table," Johnson said. "I'm excited he's here. He's a tremendous person, great personality, fits in seamlessly. He's got worlds of experience and he's an extremely hard worker. He's not kicking up his feet and telling stories. He's rolling his sleeves up and getting his hands dirty. He's going to help all of us and probably me, specifically, a ton this year."

Donovan joined the staff in July, replacing former lead assistant Sean Sweeney, who left San Antonio to take the head coaching job in Orlando. Sweeney ran the Spurs' defense last season, helping it improve from 25th to third in the NBA in defensive rating (110.4).

Donovan won't be tasked with taking on Sweeney's responsibilities, according to sources, however. San Antonio brought in Donovan to lean on his experience on both ends of the floor, as well as his vast knowledge of the NBA and college games.

A member of the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame class of 2025, Donovan joined the Spurs after 11 seasons as an NBA coach with the Chicago Bulls and Oklahoma City Thunder, after capturing two college basketball national titles in 2006 and 2007 with the Florida Gators. -- Michael C. Wright

Shead agrees to three-year extension in Toronto
Guard Jamal Shead has agreed to a three-year, $24 million extension with the Toronto Raptors, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Shead averaged 6.6 points and 5.6 assists per game last season.

Nuggets add Nembhard on two-way deal

Guard Ryan Nembhard has agreed to a two-way contract with the Denver Nuggets, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Nembhard, 23, played 60 games (27 starts) for the Dallas Mavericks in 2025-26 after signing as an undrafted free agent. He was traded to the Atlanta Hawks then to the Charlotte Hornets this offseason before being waived.

Sept. 29

Charania: NBA reviewing finalists' bids for Vegas team

ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the NBA is currently reviewing finalist bids for a new expansion team in Las Vegas. The price range is currently speculated at $12-13 billion with a new arena factored into the cost.

The three final groups are Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN.

Will KAT take a pay cut in next Knicks deal?

On "NBA Today," ESPN's Malika Andrews detailed Karl-Anthony Towns' mindset toward contract negotiations with the defending champion New York Knicks.

"Towns, from what I have been told, is willing -- similarly to what Jalen Brunson did [but the] numbers aren't the same -- to take a pay cut," Andrews said. "But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable."

Towns, 30, is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension through June 30.

Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice
Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday.

"He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see."

After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries.

He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain.

The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona, who is dealing with a sprained left foot.

Anfernee Simons, who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp.

"Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that."

Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season.

Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise.

"With any team, we got to start somewhere, and then we got to get better and better, and just keep trying to reach our ceiling, right?" Nurse said. "That happens day-to-day. Can we get up tomorrow, like, 98% as excited as we did today? It's going to be hard to get as excited as we all were today, right?

"But we need to come back, and we need to keep climbing that mountain. That's a daily process. I just want them to reach their potential. If they do, great things are going to happen." -- Dave McMenamin

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

Sept. 28

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books.

Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade

Jayson Tatum's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate.

That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship.

"The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday. "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years."

Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team
It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch.

The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%.

Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience.

Williamson not where he wants to be
New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player.
"I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be."

Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab

Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery, Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp.

"I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly."

Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon.

It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process.

A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule.

"My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater

Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham

Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals.

Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25.

"I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed."

Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season.

"I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit.

"In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard

Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham

The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move.

Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP

At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season.

"No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

"The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row.

"We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward."

ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic. No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes

Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling
Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title:

"It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is."

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year"

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key.

There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks

Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons"

At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal.

Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset.

"This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win.

"We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi

MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes
The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon.

"It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit.

"My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood."

As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon

Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles

The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season.

Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year"

Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me."

Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks
New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

stories.headline: Jake Paul cleared to fight; Canelo, Strickland, others on wish list
stories.summary: Jake Paul, who has been cleared to resume fighting after recovering from a broken jaw, has a list of big names he'd like to face in boxing and MMA now that he's back.
stories.body:
Jake Paul has been medically cleared to return to boxing.

Paul (12-2, seven KOs), 29, has not fought since he suffered a broken jaw during his knockout loss to Anthony Joshua last December. Paul underwent surgical procedures on his jaw in December and February. Nakisa Bidarian, co-founder of Paul's Most Valuable Promotions, officially updated Paul's status Thursday.

"Jake Paul has been cleared to return to the boxing ring," Bidarian wrote on X.

Paul told ESPN in April that he'd resumed light training but had not been cleared to spar. He has targeted a full return to competition in early 2027.

In connection to the update on his health, Paul provided his latest wish list of eventual fights this week. The list included 15 potential fights, including Canelo Alvarez, Ryan Garcia, Francis Ngannou, Deontay Wilder in boxing as well as mixed martial arts contests against Conor McGregor and Nate Diaz.

The list also included UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland (31-7), who linked himself to Paul this week in a series of online posts expressing frustration about his UFC contract.

"I gotta be honest, unless things change with the UFC I'm kinda over it," Strickland wrote on X. "McGregor makes 30 million to fight for 30 seconds and they don't want to pay us a fraction of it. Contemplating just going to 205 [pounds], knocking out my contract and scrapping with [Jake Paul]. That sounds fun."

Paul, who has been vocal for years along with MVP in encouraging the UFC to increase its fighter pay, acknowledged Strickland's post in a response.

"Sean Strickland I see your texts but are you out of contract?" Paul wrote. "Tell your 'promoter' to call MVP."

stories.headline: Fever's Clark denounces online hate directed at 'good soul' Mitchell
stories.summary: Caitlin Clark said she has talked with Kelsey Mitchell since her teammate spoke about online hate she has received and the difficulty of playing with the Fever.
stories.body:
Caitlin Clark held her final media session of the season Thursday and said she has talked with Kelsey Mitchell since her backcourt mate spoke about online hate she has received and the difficulty of playing with the Indiana Fever at times.

The intense attention the organization has gotten since Clark joined has attracted a vocal group that has been abusive to Fever players and others around the league.

"Showing up every day to compete for fans that may or may not like you is hard," Mitchell had said Saturday during her season-ending media session.

It "makes you upset," Clark said of what her teammate has gone through, noting that Mitchell is a "good soul." Clark denounced anyone who would spew abuse in her name but also said she appreciates the genuine fans who have supported her, the team and the organization.

"As far as people that have used me to demonstrate racist rhetoric or hate or discrimination, that's not something I stand for," Clark said. "That's never been something I've stood for. For those of you that know me, you know that's not what I'm about. It's not how I was raised, so that's really disappointing when people do that.

"I think it kind of gets into this larger discussion in mainstream sports of what people go through. I think just recently I saw Coco Gauff came out and kind of talked about her experience as well. So anytime I see something like that, [it] makes me upset, makes me sad, makes me really disappointed. Because that's not who I am. It's not what I'm about."

Retaining Mitchell, who is an unrestricted free agent after setting the WNBA single-season scoring record, is the top priority for the Fever, but she made it clear that on-court, basketball-related factors won't be the only influence on her decision. Mitchell has played all nine seasons with Indiana after being the No. 2 pick in the 2018 draft.

"For my teammates, obviously, there's a lot of really great things that come with playing here, too," Clark said. "And as far as Kelsey and our future with her, with the organization, she knows how much I love her, and we've talked since the season has ended. And there's nobody I would want to share the backcourt with other than her.

"I know this organization is, we're going to work our butt off to get her back. We're going to recruit her as hard as we can. Every player that is signed to a contract is going to recruit her as hard as we can. We need her. We love her.

"I hope for the rest of my career I get to play alongside her," Clark said.

Mitchell isn't the first player to voice her frustration with fans, particularly those associated with Indiana who crossed the line from critical to abusive. A'ja Wilson of the Aces got into an altercation with a fan during Game 2 of the postseason opening round inside Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Aces teammate Jackie Young took issue with a pair of fans sitting courtside in Indiana in August. None of those involved were found to have violated the league's fan code of conduct. Mercury forward Alyssa Thomas said she received death threats and was called racial slurs after receiving a one-game suspension for making contact with Clark's throat with her first.

General manager Amber Cox said last week that "the attacks on our fanbases have no basis in reality, and they need to stop."

Former Fever player Brianna Turner, who serves as treasurer of the Women's National Basketball Players Association, disagreed, posting on social media, "This is an unequivocally false statement."

Clark said she doesn't remember the last time she has checked her direct messages on social media, specifically to avoid all of the bitter talk.

"I just try to block out the noise the best I can," Clark said. "Obviously, I've been under this microscope with the lights bright for six years now. So you kind of figure out how to navigate it. That doesn't mean everything's easy for me. That doesn't mean there aren't moments that are hard. And that goes the same [for] players in this league, that doesn't make it easy for them. It doesn't mean that there aren't hard days. But, obviously, the WNBA has grown so much, and there's more and more eyeballs. I think for the real fans that do show up and do support and do respect, I applaud you. And there are a lot of you, and that's not just here in Indianapolis. That's across the league.

"I think there's certainly a line, and that can't be crossed," she added. "I think any of us, and any person in their right mind, know that there's certain rhetoric that's just not OK, and that's not something I've ever stood for. But at the same time, there are a lot of really great fans and a lot of fans that I really truly enjoy getting to play in front of and I'm really thankful for. And I thank them for coming out. They made it a great season and were loud every single night.

"But for me, I think just I do the best I can to block it out, block out the noise, and try to limit my time on social media the best I can."

stories.headline: Harry Kane interest in MLS 'fulfilment of a dream' - commissioner
stories.summary: MLS commissioner Don Garber would love Harry Kane to follow Lionel Messi across the pond and says the England skipper's interest helps fulfil a dream that Sir David Beckham kept alive.
stories.body:
MLS commissioner Don Garber would love Harry Kane to follow Lionel Messi across the pond and says the England skipper's interest helps fulfil a dream that Sir David Beckham kept alive.

The 33-year-old is in the running for the Ballon d'Or having scored 73 goals for club and country in a season that saw the striker win the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich before World Cup bronze.

Kane shows no signs of slowing and he marked his record-equalling 125th England appearance by extending his international goal tally to 91 in Tuesday's 3-0 Nations League win against Czechia.

The striker scored six goals across a four-match camp that began with him revealing his interest in eventually moving to MLS as the striker spoke about his dreams of being an NFL kicker.

"I'd love for him to do that," commissioner Garber said. "I think, for me, it is the fulfilment of the dream that we had to build a proper soccer league that would drive a soccer nation. That sounds colloquial but actually we have that written down.

"We wanted to create something that would have the Harry Kanes of the world say 'I'd kind of like to play in MLS.' And I think Messi proved that.

"That was a competitive process, working to ensure that we had a dynamic that would be better than going back to Barca, working a dynamic that would not have him want to play in Saudi Arabia.

"Play in Miami, have them be able to build a new stadium and have him set records and be an MVP, and then have an unbelievable goodbye [this week] from his international career."

Garber welcomes Kane's keenness to move to MLS and is eternally grateful to another England captain as he prepares to step down from the post of commissioner he has held since 1999.

Beckham's move to LA Galaxy acted as the catalyst for the league's growth, which only accelerated when the former midfielder helped form Inter Miami and sign Argentina great Messi in 2023.

"I don't think I would say one is more important than the other," Garber said of the star duo's impact.

"David put this league on the path to credibility and respect. In the prime of his career, he came to LA.

"He came into Major League Soccer and showed the world that this league can be competitive, it could be respected, it could be fun, it could have great players.

"It attracted [Thierry] Henry and many, many other players right after that, so without David there's probably no Major League Soccer.

"That being said, Major League Soccer would not be the global phenomenon and not be sort of on the hearts and minds of just about anybody in the world without Leo Messi."

Garber will become chairman at the turn of the year and is proud of his legacy with MLS, which was founded as part of the bid to hold the 1994 World Cup in a country that has just co-hosted the largest edition of the tournament.

- England Nations League takeaways: Kane makes history, Tuchel steadies ship

The 68-year-old says they have made the planet's "biggest commercial market for the sport" during that time and is excited to see how they build on firm foundations.

"We just went from a country road, now we're getting onto the highway," Garber told the Press Association. "And we've got to get better.

"We have to have a league that is more competitive, that has an ability to get into the Club World Cup and win games. Miami won one.

"Not just be there but have people think that an MLS team can compete against other clubs in the world."

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: With an 84-point lead in the drivers' standings, it is looking increasingly likely that Kimi Antonelli will be crowned F1's youngest world champion in the next two months.
stories.body:
With an 84-point lead in the drivers' standings, it is looking increasingly likely that Kimi Antonelli will be crowned F1's youngest world champion in the next two months.

Determining when and where that coronation will likely take place is much harder to say, not least because there are still question marks over how many races remain in the F1 calendar.

Antonelli's closest competitor, Mercedes teammate George Russell, saw his title chances take a critical blow when he retired from Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia with an engine failure, and a related grid penalty at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix will make his job tougher still.

Meanwhile, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc, Lando Norris and Max Verstappen all remain in mathematical contention for this year's championship, but face even tougher routes to the title than Russell due to their greater points deficits.

When could Antonelli win his first title?
In theory, the earliest Antonelli could seal the title is at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin later this month. In order to do so, he would need to grow his gap over Russell by 42 points in two race weekends, while outscoring Lewis Hamilton in third place by 20 points.

- Singapore Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch

- Valtteri Bottas cycles 400km from Malaysia to Singapore

- F1 cars to get software update after Malaysia 'bug'

Even with extra points on offer at the sprint race in Singapore this weekend, such a scenario would likely require victories for Antonelli and further retirements for Russell, while ensuring Hamilton is not in the fight for second place on the podium behind Antonelli. In addition, an Austin crowning would require Antonelli to make sure he is not outscored by three points by Leclerc, and six points by both Norris and Verstappen.

What does Antonelli need to claim the title?
Perhaps the easiest way to look at Antonelli's title run-in is that he needs to score 100 points over the remaining races to ensure he ends up as champion -- regardless of what any of his rivals manage.

With seven grands prix and a sprint race currently scheduled on the calendar, that route could be achieved with multiple different result combinations -- but for ease of an example, third place at every remaining race would comfortably see Antonelli over the line even if Russell wins at all seven grands prix and the sprint.

F1's rules state that if multiple drivers are tied on points, a countback of victories will decide who emerges on top. If the number of victories are also even, it then goes to second places, third places, fourth place, and so on. Currently, Antonelli has eight victories to Russell's three, although Russell has four second places to Antonelli's three. It's unlikely those countbacks will come into play, but it's why, currently, Antonelli needs 100 points rather than 99 to put the title entirely beyond Russell's grasp.

But how many races are actually left?
The situation is further complicated by question marks hanging over the final two races of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. F1 has made clear that it intends to finish the season as scheduled, but the ongoing war between the United States and Iran has the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

The same conflict led the cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in April, while Bahrain took the unusual approach of hosting its round 4,000 miles away from the island kingdom in Malaysia last weekend.

If Qatar and Abu Dhabi are also cancelled, F1's contingency plan is to host the final round of the season in Imola. Such a scenario would remove 25 of the potential points on offer, meaning Antonelli would only need 75 points between now and the end of the season to be crowned champion. Austin would still be the earliest round at which he could clinch the title, but it would come with a more achievable target of outscoring Russell by 17 points across the Singapore and U.S. race weekends rather than 42.

stories.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'I still have the scar' from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.

The Spaniard, whose new four-year contract at the Emirates was announced on Wednesday, took the club to their first Champions League final for 20 years last season but saw his team defeated on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Echoing the words of the last man to take them to the brink of elite European glory -- Arsène Wenger, who previously said that "every defeat is a scar in your heart" -- Arteta told The Athletic: "I still have the scar, like Arsène says.

"I still have that poison in my veins. It has to stay there because that's when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody."

Looking towards the future, Arteta added that he was excited for a number of different aspects of the club's growth.

"Globally, with our supporters? Great. How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we're going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great," he said.

"But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite."

He added: "It feels like it's still a lot to do, and it's just the beginning."

Arteta has, however, already managed to do something no Arsenal manager had achieved for 22 years: win a league title.

"It wasn't just a trophy. It was a moment that we're going to remember for the rest of our lives," he said.

Asked what game from his Arsenal tenure he would relive, the 44-year-old chose the controversial 1-0 win over West Ham which put the Gunners on the brink of returning to the top of the perch.

"This is football elevated to its best version, when a journey, a moment that can change so many people's lives, goes one way or the other," he said. "You just pray because you know if it goes the wrong side, probably it's gone again.

"That day when I went home, I said, 'We're going to be champions. It is our year. This has happened for a reason, and we're going to get it done.'"

Arsenal return from the international break in Saturday's early kickoff against Leeds United at the Emirates, looking to return to the top of the table ahead of Manchester City's trip to Liverpool on Sunday.
